messages:
Morgan: trying to set up an A/B in Console for the new 8-bit quant kernel. goal: 5% traffic to canary, auto-roll back if p95 > 250ms OR error_rate > 0.5% over a 5m window. Console UI looks thin for compound guards — anyone implemented this pattern?
Sara: we did a variant of this for the tokenizer swap. backend already supports multiple guard clauses and lookback windows, but the editor only exposes one metric + threshold today.
Devin: we should support boolean ops and grouping, e.g. (p95_latency > 250ms AND error_rate > 0.5%) OR upstream_429s > 1%. lookback: 5m, eval cadence: 1m. example config we used:```json
{
  "experiment_id":"exp-quant-canary-2026-03",
  "variants":[{"name":"stable","weight":95},{"name":"canary","weight":5}],
  "guards":[{
    "expr":"p95_latency > 250 AND error_rate > 0.005",
    "window":"5m",
    "action":"abort"
  }],
  "evaluation_interval":"1m"
}
```
Liam: one thing to watch: routing happens at the edge-router layer. weights are applied after route selection in most flows; if you want per-customer holdout you need to apply bucketing earlier (client id hash). checks for guard-triggered rollback are done asynchronously by the control plane which can flip weights and trigger a redeploy fallback.
Morgan: good call — we need a picker that can do both: route-by-customer for feature flags, and route-by-traffic for global canaries. Console should surface both options.
Sara: also add "per-user quota" on canary variant so a single tenant can't exhaust it. simple config: `quota: {"per_user_per_min": 5}` — we used that in the billing experiment.
Devin: telemetry wise, we must tag traces and metrics with `experiment_id` and `variant`. otherwise evals and dashboards can't attribute regressions. console should auto-create a Grafana row + PromQL templates when an experiment is created.
Morgan: is there a lightweight preview mode in Console? want to preview how traffic will split and what rollout timeline looks like before saving.
Sara: not yet. we have a naive simulator in the backend that takes weights + user segments and prints expected qps per variant. We could wire a preview button to call it and show a percentile table.
Devin: UX note: abort action should be reversible via a cooldown. e.g., after abort the canary weight goes to 0 for 10m and then requires manual re-enable. prevents flip-flopping.
Liam: routing API contract question: how should SDKs honor experiments? client SDK should only be able to read preferred variant header from proxy; actual bucketing must remain server-side to avoid client divergence.
Morgan: agree. we should document SDK semantics in the Console creation flow so product engineers know what's client-visible.
qa-bot: scheduled test run: canary-smoke-suite against canary variant in staging at 2026-03-05T18:00Z.
infra-bot: experiment created: exp-quant-canary-2026-03 by Morgan (id: exp-7892). default telemetry tags added.
Sara: next steps: I can spike a guard-UI mock with expression builder (AND/OR, windows, actions). Devin can draft the config JSON schema and open API change. Morgan will wire the preview call into Console. Liam to validate edge-router changes for early bucketing.
Morgan: thanks — @Sara @Devin @Liam I'll send a short RFC + PR checklist. want to keep the Console flow under 3 clicks for basic canaries and an "advanced" tab for boolean guards.
Devin: one more: add an emergency abort API endpoint that sets weight=0 and appends an audit reason. fast rollback is critical.
Morgan: agreed. I'll include that in the RFC.
Sara: :thumbsup:
Liam: good plan.
Morgan: filing PR in a few hours, please review when you get a chance.
